prompt.context: Our client, Greg Wilkinson, is the Dean of the business school at a mid-sized, four-year university. They are experiencing declining application rates and have brought us in to help determine the reason for the decline and how to bolster converted admissions. He must present to the Board of Visitors on the topic later this week.
prompt.question: What is driving the decline in application rates, and how can Greg Wilkinson bolster converted admissions for his business school?

clarifying_info.a: Application rate is the number of applicants to the university. Schools like to see this number grow, indicating preference and prestige of the school.
Converted admissions is the number of applicants who have been offered admission to the school and accept that offer to attend.

clarifying_info.q: Why does Greg Wilkinson want to pursue this?
clarifying_info.a: Schools need tuition dollars of a certain threshold to cover their operating budget, so a decline in quality, interested prospective students (i.e. declining application rates) makes that threshold more difficult to reach.

clarifying_info.q: What is the business model for a university?
clarifying_info.a: Universities receive revenue mainly through tuition dollars and endowment donations. They have a large set of fixed operating costs to cover, so budgets are typically tight.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current state of the education industry?
clarifying_info.a: More information will be provided later in the case.
He wants to increase converted admissions to drive tuition dollars.

exhibits.title: Number of High School Students Pursuing Secondary Education by Category
exhibits.shows: A table showing the number of high school graduates (in millions) pursuing different categories of secondary education in 2015 and 2020.

exhibits.title: Cost and Impact Information for Experiential Education Program
exhibits.shows: A summary of the key financial and operational parameters for a proposed experiential education program from Cavalier & Co.

data.note: Converted Admissions Offers is defined as the % of admitted students that attend the program

framework: Student Value: quality of education, student experience, prestige of program, career opportunities, cost of attendance, likelihood of scholarship
University Financials: tuition revenue, endowment/donations, scholarships, faculty/staff salary, operating costs, capital expenditures
Industry Trends & Competition: number of students attending secondary institutions, 2-year vs. 4-year programs vs. trade school, online vs. in-person education, COVID impacts

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, what is the overall trend in secondary education? Which category is most threatening to Greg Wilkinson's program?
questions.guidance: A good candidate recognizes the overall secondary education market is growing (from 4.0M to 5.0M). A great candidate also notes that while the absolute number of 4-year residential applicants is rising, the residential universities' percentage share is declining. All online options are gaining share, making them the primary competitive threat.

math.setup: Sum all categories for 2015 and 2020, then calculate each category's percentage share.
math.answer: The total secondary education market grew from 4.0M to 5.0M students (+25%). However, residential universities (both 4-year and 2-year) lost market share, while online universities and MOOCs gained share. Online and MOOC categories are the primary competitive threat.

questions.prompt: Greg Wilkinson has been approached by Cavalier & Co. about designing a comprehensive experiential education program (simulations, mentorship, curriculum changes) for $3.4MM. University policy requires a payback period of 4 years or less. Using Exhibit 2 and the additional data provided, should Greg move forward?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for current enrollment data before calculating. A good candidate ties back to the 4-year payback policy. A great candidate recognizes that the tuition increase grows each year as the 2% conversion improvement compounds across successive admissions classes (Year 1: +200 students, Year 2: +400, Year 3: +600, Year 4: +800).

math.setup: Admitted students = Applications * Acceptance Rate. Additional converted students = Admitted * 2% increase. New tuition = Additional students * $40K. Funds available to business school = New tuition * 5%. Cumulative payback over 4 years.
steps: Funds available to business school per year = $8,000,000 * 5% = $400,000
Year 3 cumulative: $1,200,000 + $1,200,000 = $2,400,000 (note: each new cohort adds another 200 students)
$4.0MM > $3.4MM cost, so payback is achieved within 4 years
math.answer: Yes, Greg should move forward. Cumulative tuition available over 4 years is $4.0MM, which exceeds the $3.4MM program cost. The program pays back within the university's 4-year policy requirement. Additional info needed from candidate: current applications = 50,000; acceptance rate = 20%; current admissions offer conversion = 3%.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some ways that Greg Wilkinson's school can combat the competition from online education categories?

categories.name: Integrate Technology into Traditional Classroom
ideas: Incorporate pre-recorded videos on specific topics
Use interactive platforms like polls and Wordles in class

categories.name: Leverage Power of In-Person Relationships
ideas: Do more project-based and discussion-based work versus lectures
Partner with professionals in the field for shadowing opportunities
Leverage alumni and professors for 1:1 mentor relationships

categories.name: Strategically Introduce Online Classes
ideas: Make lower credit-hour classes available at-your-own-pace
Integrate Coursera-type classes to cover fundamental topics ahead of school start

recommendation: Greg Wilkinson should pursue creating an experiential education program with Cavalier & Co. to combat competition from online school offerings. It will add a real-world component to the classroom, offering diversity in experiences.
The project meets the university's 4-year payback policy, with cumulative tuition funds of $4.0MM exceeding the $3.4MM program cost.
risks: The experiential education program will be a heavy operational lift for Greg's school to integrate and operationalize.
Estimates of the 2% increase in converted admissions may be inflated, which would extend the payback period beyond 4 years.
next_steps: Promote use of simulation to prospective students to drive application interest.
Create a training program for professors and school administrators on new experiential methods.
Develop a detailed integration plan and timeline for rolling out the program.
Conduct market research to confirm payback period assumptions and refine conversion rate estimates.
